children: The South African rand fell sharply on Monday as renewed supply disruptions in the Middle East pushed oil prices higher, adding pressure on the currency, while investors looked ahead to the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy meeting later this week for clues on the interest rate outlook.
At 1337 GMT the rand traded at 16.3175 against the dollar
, roughly down 1.1% from its previous close.
Oil prices rose more than 3% on Monday, after new strikes on Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure and attacks on ships in the Middle East compounded supply concerns.
This has weighed on the South African currency, as the country is a net importer of oil and therefore vulnerable to rising crude prices.
, South Africa's key export, was down 1.2% at $4,296.68 per ounce by 1216 GMT.
Investors are closely watching Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision for clues on the interest rate outlook and whether pressure on the rand could intensify.

"The more important signal on Wednesday won't be the probability of a 25 basis points hike, it'll be the guidance that follows, and whether Chair Kevin Warsh can convince markets the Fed is still serious about fighting inflation even as oil drags it higher," said ETM Analytics.
On the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, the Top-40 index
South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond (ZAR2035=) also weakened, with the yield rising 6.5 basis points to 8.8%.
